reports.title: Doomsday Cult Leader Paul MacKenzie's Sentencing In Shakahola Massacre
reports.description: Paul Mackenzie was convicted alongside 28 other suspects in the murder of 128 children and one adult in a Massacre that left more than 400 people dead at Shakahola forest in Chains.

reports.title: Paul Mackenzie sentenced to 200 years in prison for Shakahola massacre.
reports.description:
Pastor Paul Mackenzie has been sentenced to 200 years in prison over the Shakahola massacre. The case examines his individual criminal culpability and why he bears primary responsibility for the deaths. As the overall leader of Good News International (GNI) Ministries and the Shakahola settlement, Mackenzie orchestrated the move into the wilderness, presided over meetings where followers were directed to fast to death, and specifically targeted children as the first victims.

The discussion further explores the disturbing allegations surrounding the burials of victims, which Mackenzie reportedly referred to as weddings, the directives issued to village elders, and the alleged use of violence against children who resisted fasting, attempted to stop or sought to escape. It examines the different degrees of responsibility and participation in the Shakahola tragedy, raising critical questions about religious authority, abuse of trust, criminal accountability and the protection of vulnerable followers.

reports.title: Paul Mackenzie Arrives in Court Under Heavy Security Ahead of Shakahola Massacre Sentencing
reports.description:
Doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie has arrived in court under tight security ahead of his sentencing over the Shakahola massacre.

Mackenzie made his court appearance accompanied by his co-convicts, with security officers maintaining a heavy presence as the group was escorted into the court premises.

The arrival comes as the court prepares to deliver its sentence in the case arising from the Shakahola massacre, one of Kenya's most shocking tragedies.

Mackenzie, who is at the centre of the case, has faced accusations linked to the deaths of hundreds of people whose bodies were discovered in mass graves in Shakahola, Kilifi County.

reports.title: Preacher Paul Mackenzie and 28 Co-Accused Found Guilty in Shakahola Massacre Murder Trial
reports.description:
Paul Mackenzie and 29 co-accused have been found guilty and convicted on all 191 counts of murder in the Shakahola massacre trial. Justice Diana Kavedza presided over the proceedings at the Mombasa High Court, delivering a landmark judgment in the case linked to the deaths of followers who were allegedly subjected to a deadly fasting regime.

The court examined evidence detailing how children and other followers were denied food and water, beaten for resisting the fasting directive and punished for attempting to escape. The judgment marks a major development in the case arising from the Shakahola tragedy.

reports.title: DPP Renson Igonga, Deputy DCI John Onyango in Court for Shakahola Massacre Judgment
Paul Mackenzie and co-accused Arriving at Mombasa Law Courts Ahead of Shakahola Massacre Judgment
reports.description:
Self-proclaimed preacher Paul Nthenge Mackenzie and his co-accused have arrived at Mombasa Law Courts ahead of the highly anticipated judgment in the Shakahola massacre case. Mackenzie and his co-accused face 191 counts of murder linked to the deaths of 191 children whose bodies were recovered from mass graves in Shakahola Forest, Kilifi County.

The judgment follows a lengthy trial in which the prosecution presented testimony from 121 witnesses, including survivors, investigators and experts. The court’s decision is expected to determine the fate of the accused in one of Kenya’s most shocking cases involving alleged religious extremism and mass deaths

reports.title: Media Helped the World Know the Truth’ — Pastor Ezekiel on Shakahola
reports.description: Pastor Ezekiel, speaking at Kilifi International School, said the media played a crucial role in telling the world the truth about his church during the period he says he was persecuted following the Shakahola massacre. He commended journalists and media houses for their critical role in informing the public and shaping society.

reports.title: Shakahola Drama: Lawyer Presses DCI Officer to show Mackenzie’s link to the deaths
reports.description: In the ongoing Shakahola case, Pastor Paul Mackenzie’s lawyer cross-examines a DCI officer who earlier testified on Mackenzie’s alleged role in the deaths linked to the Shakahola tragedy. The defense presses the officer to substantiate how the investigation connects Mackenzie to the deaths of his followers.

reports.title: Shakahola: Shock in Court as Man buried by family Appears Alive Before Justice Mochache
reports.description: Moses Karema also known as Sharifu being produced  before Justice Diana Mochache at the Mombasa High Court in Mombasa County on Wednesday 5th November 2025, during the hearing in a matter where controversial preacher Paul Makenzi and 29 others are facing 191 counts of murder.  Moses confirmed to the high court that he was indeed Sharifu, the same person his father on Tuesday claimed he was dead and buried. Moses is detained at Shimo la Tewa Prisons in a different Shakahola case.

reports.title: Lawyer Grills Former Malindi OCS on Whether Refusing to Eat Means Fasting in Shakahola Case Hearing
reports.description: Former Malindi OCS Ali Noor Abdi hard pressed by Controversial preacher Paul Makenzi's lawyer Lawrence Obonyo to explain if refusal to eat simply means fasting during a hearing  at Shanzu Law Court in Mombasa County, where Makenzi and other accused persons are facing terror charges.

reports.title: Tanzanian Father Whose Child Died in Shakahola Clashes With Mackenzie’s Lawyer in Court
reports.description: A Tanzanian father whose child died in the Shakahola forest cult ordeal clashed in court with Mackenzie’s lawyer over accountability in the mass-death case led by Paul Mackenzie. He appeared before the court, emotionally recounting how his family joined the cult, the forced fasting, and the tragic loss of his child. The confrontation highlights the human toll of the famine-based ritual and the ongoing legal battle to secure justice for the victims.

reports.title: Pastor Paul Mackenzie Says There Was an Assassination Plot Against Him in Prison
reports.description: Controversial preacher Paul Makenzi, the main suspect in the Shakahola massacre, has claimed there was an attempt on his life at Shimo la Tewa Prisons. Appearing before Justice Diana Mochache, Makenzi alleged “bad blood” with the prison head and said he faces intimidation and harassment from officers. His lawyers urged the court to ensure his safety or transfer him to another facility. The judge ordered the claims to be recorded and investigated by the Kenya Prisons Service. Makenzi faces multiple counts of murder, manslaughter, and radicalization over the Shakahola deaths.

reports.title: Pastor Mackenzie’s Lawyer Puts Up Spirited Fight in Court as He Questions Witness
reports.description: Pastor Paul Mackenzie’s lawyer put up a spirited fight in court as he cross-examined a witness in the ongoing Shakahola massacre trial. Mackenzie, leader of Good News International Ministries, was arrested in 2023 after over 429 bodies were exhumed from Shakahola Forest, Kilifi, where followers were allegedly coerced to starve to death. He faces charges including murder, manslaughter, terrorism, and child abuse alongside dozens of co-accused.

reports.title: Shakahola Horror: Woman Recounts How Her two Sisters and their 10 Children got lost in Cult Massacre
reports.description: A woman has given heartbreaking testimony, recounting how her two sisters and their 10 children perished in the Shakahola cult massacre. The tragedy unfolded in 2023, when followers of preacher Paul Nthenge Mackenzie, leader of Good News International Ministries, were lured into mass starvation in Shakahola Forest, Kilifi. Mackenzie was later arrested and, together with dozens of co-accused, now faces charges including murder, manslaughter, terrorism, and child abuse. The case is currently in court, where witnesses continue to give harrowing accounts of how families were lost in Kenya’s deadliest cult tragedy. The hearing continues as the full scale of the massacre is laid bare.

reports.title: Controversial Preacher Paul Mackenzie Appearing in Court for His Manslaughter Case
reports.description: Controversial preacher Paul Mackenzie appeared in court for his manslaughter case, but the hearing failed to proceed before Justice Kavedza. The prosecution sought an adjournment to align their file and finalize amendments to the charges. Justice Kavedza expressed displeasure at the slow pace of the case and the adjournment, noting that significant public resources had already been used to set up the hearing. The matter was adjourned to Wednesday to allow the prosecution to complete the amendments.

reports.title: Government Analyst Who Helped in Exhumation of Bodies in Shakahola Testifies
reports.description: Government Analyst David Mumbao, who played a key role in the Shakahola massacre investigations, testified in court today on the procedures followed during the exhumation of over 400 bodies from shallow graves linked to cult leader Paul Mackenzie. Mumbao detailed the forensic methods used and the condition of the remains recovered from the forest in Kilifi County.

reports.title: Malindi Children officer Sebastian Muteti testifies in Pastor Paul Mackenzie Shakahola case
reports.description: Sebastian Muteti’s testimony painted a harrowing picture of systematic child abuse carried out under Pastor Mackenzie’s Shakahola cult. His accounts of starvation, torture, and radical indoctrination among minors deepen the weight of the charges as the trial continues, highlighting the role of civil protection agencies amid a complex criminal investigation.

reports.title: “Hata kama Mackenzie anaonekana shetani mkubwa...” Pastor Mackenzie says
reports.description: Controversial preacher Paul Makenzi and other accused persons during a break at the Mombasa Law Court in Mombasa County on Tuesday 29th July 2025, during the hearing in a matter where he is accused alongside 92 other persons with 238 counts of manslaughter.
